verses.text: "'When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you must set apart a holy portion of the land as a gift to the LORD. It will be twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide. The whole area will be holy.
Out of this, a square five hundred cubits long and five hundred cubits wide will be for the sanctuary, with an open area fifty cubits wide all around it.
In this holy area, measure off a section twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide. The sanctuary, the most holy place, will be in it.
It will be the holy portion of the land for the priests who serve in the sanctuary and come near to serve the LORD. It will be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
Another area, twenty-five thousand cubits long and ten thousand cubits wide, will belong to the Levites who serve in the temple. It will be their own land for towns to live in.
"'Next to the holy portion, you must give the city an area five thousand cubits wide and twenty-five thousand cubits long. It will belong to all the people of Israel.

"'The prince will have the land on both sides of the holy portion and the city's land, bordering them both. It will stretch west from the west side and east from the east side, running from the western border to the eastern border, as long as one of the tribal portions.
This land will be his property in Israel. Then my princes will no longer oppress my people. They will let the people of Israel have the rest of the land by their tribes.
"'This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough, you princes of Israel! Stop your violence and robbery, and do what is right and fair. Stop driving my people off their land, says the Lord GOD.
You must use honest scales, an honest ephah for dry measure, and an honest bath for liquid measure.
The ephah and the bath must be the same size. The bath will hold one tenth of a homer, and the ephah will hold one tenth of a homer. The homer will be the standard for both.
The shekel will be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels will make one mina.
"'This is the offering you must give: one sixth of an ephah from every homer of wheat, and one sixth of an ephah from every homer of barley.
The set amount of olive oil, measured by the bath, is one tenth of a bath from every cor. A cor is ten baths, the same as a homer, since ten baths make a homer.

Also give one sheep from every flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel. These will be used for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, to make the people right with God, says the Lord GOD.
All the people of the land must give this offering to the prince of Israel.

It will be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the festivals, the New Moons, the Sabbaths, and all the appointed festivals of Israel. He will provide the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make the people of Israel right with God.
"'This is what the Lord GOD says: On the first day of the first month, take a young bull with nothing wrong with it and purify the sanctuary.

The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the upper ledge of the altar, and on the gateposts of the inner courtyard.
Do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins by mistake or without knowing it. This is how you will make the temple right.
"'On the fourteenth day of the first month, you must celebrate the Passover, a festival lasting seven days. During it you must eat bread made without yeast.
On that day the prince must provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
Every day during the seven days of the festival, he must provide seven bulls and seven rams with nothing wrong with them as a burnt offering to the LORD, and a male goat as a sin offering.
He must provide a grain offering of one ephah for each bull and one ephah for each ram, along with a hin of olive oil for each ephah.
"'During the festival that begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he must provide the same things for seven days: the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and olive oil.
